_comment: Hand-authored metadata layered on top of curriculum.json. Subject numbers are the numbers used in the source syllabus. 'prereq' = should be understood first; 'related' = useful cross-links. Edit here, then run tools/build.py.

1.title: Computer Science Foundations
1.scope: How computers represent information, how hardware executes programs, and the mathematics, operating-system and networking ideas that every later subject assumes.

2.title: Programming and Software Development
2.scope: Writing programs well: fundamentals, paradigms, language ecosystems, data structures and algorithms, and how compilers turn source code into running software.

3.title: Professional Software Engineering
3.scope: The discipline around the code: lifecycle models, requirements, design principles and patterns, architecture, version control, tooling and documentation.

4.title: Building Software Products
4.scope: The components of a product: databases, backends, APIs, frontends, mobile and desktop applications, user experience, and system integration.

5.title: Distributed Systems and System Design
5.scope: What changes when software runs on many machines, and how to design systems that stay correct, available and scalable.

6.title: Cloud, DevOps and Infrastructure
6.scope: Running software in production: cloud platforms, containers, delivery pipelines, reliability engineering, observability and performance.

7.title: Software Quality and Cybersecurity
7.scope: Showing software is correct and keeping it safe: testing, quality engineering, security fundamentals, cryptography and secure development.

8.title: Data Engineering, Data Science and Analytics
8.scope: Moving, storing, processing and analysing data at scale, from pipelines and streaming to statistics and business intelligence.

9.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
9.scope: A single progression from mathematics and statistics through classical machine learning, deep learning, language and vision, to LLMs, RAG, agents, MLOps and AI safety.

10.title: Specialized Software Engineering Domains
10.scope: Domains with their own bodies of knowledge: games and graphics, spatial computing, embedded systems, IoT, robotics, blockchain, HPC, quantum computing and more.

11.title: AI-Assisted Software Engineering
11.scope: How AI coding assistants and agents change the way software is written, reviewed, tested and maintained, and the responsibilities that stay with the engineer.

12.title: Professional Engineering Practices
12.scope: Standards, release management, engineering economics, ethics and law, communication and leadership, and the research-level computer science behind the field.

13.title: Complete Technology Ecosystem
13.scope: An index of the tools, platforms and technology families a software engineer may encounter. It is a map, not a list of things everyone must install.

14.title: How the Entire Field Fits Together
14.scope: How the layers of computing depend on each other, from foundations through applications and infrastructure to data, intelligence and frontier computing.

15.title: Practical Learning Order
15.scope: A realistic order for learning, and a clear distinction between generalist foundations and specialist depth.

1.summary: What a computer is, how numbers, text and media are represented as bits, how Boolean logic underlies computation, what each hardware component does, and how a processor executes instructions. Every later subject uses this vocabulary.
outcomes: Explain the input, processing, output and storage model and the hardware/software boundary
Convert between binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal and do two's-complement arithmetic by hand
Explain IEEE 754 and why 0.1 + 0.2 is not exactly 0.3, and how text is encoded in ASCII and Unicode
Trace one instruction through the fetch-decode-execute cycle
projects: A base-conversion and bit-inspection toolkit in Python
A hex-dump utility in C
A simulated 8-bit ALU built from logic gates

2.summary: The mathematical toolkit behind algorithms, graphics, cryptography, AI and quantum computing: discrete mathematics, logic, graph theory, linear algebra, probability, statistics, calculus and numerical methods.
outcomes: Write and critique proofs by induction, contradiction and contrapositive
Count with permutations, combinations and recurrences
Compute with vectors and matrices and interpret eigenvalues, probability distributions and gradients
projects: Matrix operations and Gaussian elimination from scratch
Monte Carlo simulations of probability puzzles

3.summary: From transistors and logic gates to combinational and sequential circuits, datapaths, instruction sets, pipelining, caches and modern processor architectures.
outcomes: Design combinational and sequential circuits from gates and flip-flops
Describe a CPU datapath, control unit and instruction set, and compare RISC with CISC
Explain pipeline hazards and how the cache hierarchy shapes performance
projects: A software simulator for a small CPU
A cache simulator that reports hit rates for access traces

4.summary: How an operating system manages processes, memory, files, devices and concurrency, and how those mechanisms shape every program that runs on top of it.
outcomes: Explain processes, threads, scheduling and context switches
Explain virtual memory, paging and file systems
Recognise and prevent race conditions and deadlocks
projects: A small Unix shell in C
A page-replacement algorithm simulator

5.summary: How machines communicate: network models, IP addressing and routing, TCP and UDP, application protocols such as HTTP and DNS, network infrastructure, wireless networking and advanced topics.
outcomes: Trace a request from browser to server across the layers of the network stack
Explain how TCP provides reliability and how DNS, TLS and HTTP fit together
Diagnose connectivity problems with standard tools
projects: A TCP echo server and client
A minimal HTTP/1.1 server built on sockets

6.summary: The concepts common to almost every language: variables, control flow, functions, basic data structures, error handling and the first advanced ideas.
outcomes: Decompose a problem and express the solution as a program
Use functions, collections and error handling idiomatically
Read and debug unfamiliar code
projects: A command-line task manager
A text-adventure engine

7.summary: The different ways programs can be organised: imperative, procedural, object-oriented, functional, declarative, concurrent, reactive and others, with object-oriented and functional programming covered in depth.
outcomes: Identify the paradigm a codebase uses and its trade-offs
Apply object-oriented and functional techniques appropriately
Choose a paradigm that fits a problem
projects: The same program written in three paradigms
A small immutable-data library in a functional style

8.summary: The major languages and what each is used for, with their runtimes, package managers, tooling and language-specific advanced topics.
outcomes: Match languages to problem domains
Explain typing, memory-management and execution models across languages
Learn a new language efficiently by mapping it to known concepts
projects: One small service implemented in two languages and compared
A benchmark of the same algorithm across languages

9.summary: Complexity analysis, the core data structures (arrays, lists, hash tables, trees, heaps, graphs), classic and advanced algorithms, algorithmic techniques and the theory of computation behind them.
outcomes: Analyse time and space complexity
Implement and choose among core data structures with reasoned trade-offs
Apply sorting, searching, dynamic programming, greedy and graph algorithms
projects: Core data structures from scratch with a test suite
An autocomplete service built on a trie
A route planner using Dijkstra's algorithm

10.summary: How source code becomes executable behaviour: lexing, parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate representations, optimisation, code generation, interpreters and virtual machines.
outcomes: Describe each phase of a compiler pipeline
Build a lexer and parser for a small language
Explain common optimisations and runtime systems
projects: An expression parser and evaluator
A bytecode virtual machine for a tiny language

11.summary: The whole life of a software product: initiation, requirements engineering, development models, project management and maintenance.
outcomes: Write testable requirements and user stories
Compare waterfall, iterative and agile models
Plan, estimate and track a project
projects: A requirements document and backlog for a small product
A retrospective on an open-source project's release history

12.summary: Design principles, SOLID, object-oriented design, the Gang of Four patterns, architectural patterns, domain-driven design, quality attributes and architecture documentation.
outcomes: Apply SOLID and recognise when a pattern helps or harms
Choose an architectural style against quality-attribute requirements
Document an architecture so others can use it
projects: Refactor a legacy module towards a clean architecture
A decision log (ADRs) for a small system

13.summary: Git from first commit to advanced history manipulation, hosting platforms, branching strategies, pull requests and collaborative workflows.
outcomes: Use branches, merges and rebases confidently
Recover from mistakes using the reflog and reset
Run a pull-request based team workflow
projects: Contribute a documentation fix to an open-source project
A branching strategy for a small team

14.summary: The command line, editors and IDEs, debuggers and utilities, build systems and documentation tooling that make an engineer productive.
outcomes: Work fluently in a Unix shell
Debug with a debugger rather than print statements alone
Set up a reproducible build
projects: A dotfiles repository and setup script
A Makefile or CMake build for a multi-file project

15.summary: Relational and non-relational databases: SQL, schema design, indexing and storage internals, transactions and isolation, scaling, and the major database technologies.
outcomes: Model data and write correct, efficient SQL
Explain indexes, query plans and transaction isolation
Choose between relational, document, key-value and other stores
projects: A normalised schema with migrations for a small application
A key-value store with a write-ahead log

16.summary: Server-side engineering: request handling, business logic, API design, authentication and authorisation, advanced backend concerns and the major backend frameworks.
outcomes: Design and implement a REST API with validation and error handling
Implement authentication and authorisation correctly
Reason about caching, background jobs and scaling
projects: A REST API with authentication and tests
A URL shortener with rate limiting

17.summary: Browser-based user interfaces: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, major frameworks, the frontend ecosystem and advanced frontend engineering.
outcomes: Build accessible, responsive pages with semantic HTML and modern CSS
Explain how the browser parses, lays out and paints a page
Structure a component-based application with TypeScript
projects: A responsive, accessible portfolio page
A single-page application consuming a public API

18.summary: How people interact with software: user research, interaction design, usability, accessibility, visual design and evaluation methods.
outcomes: Run a basic usability test and act on the findings
Apply accessibility guidelines
Prototype and critique interface designs
projects: A clickable prototype with a usability report
An accessibility audit of an existing website

19.summary: Mobile fundamentals, Android and iOS development, cross-platform approaches and advanced mobile engineering.
outcomes: Explain the mobile application lifecycle and its constraints
Build a native or cross-platform app with local storage and networking
Handle permissions, offline use and releases
projects: A notes app with offline sync
A small app published to a test track

20.summary: Native and cross-platform desktop applications, their UI toolkits, packaging, distribution and update mechanisms.
outcomes: Choose a desktop framework for a given product
Package and distribute an application
Manage state and threading in a GUI
projects: A cross-platform text utility
An auto-updating desktop tool

21.summary: Connecting systems: integration patterns, API styles, message brokers, events, queues and the technologies that implement them.
outcomes: Choose between synchronous APIs and asynchronous messaging
Design idempotent, versioned integrations
Handle retries, ordering and failure in messaging
projects: A producer/consumer pipeline over a message broker
A webhook receiver with signature verification

22.summary: What changes when computation spans machines: partial failure, time, replication, consistency models, consensus, distributed databases and distributed architectures.
outcomes: State the CAP theorem and its limits precisely
Explain how replication and consensus protocols such as Raft work
Reason about failure modes and consistency guarantees
projects: A replicated key-value store using Raft
A fault-injection test harness for a toy service

23.summary: Designing whole systems: low-level (class and component) design, high-level architecture, capacity planning, common design patterns and advanced scenarios.
outcomes: Turn vague requirements into an architecture with justified trade-offs
Do back-of-the-envelope capacity estimates
Present and defend a design
projects: A design document for a chat system
A distributed cache design with an implementation sketch

24.summary: Cloud fundamentals and infrastructure, the three major providers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), other ecosystems and advanced cloud engineering.
outcomes: Explain IaaS, PaaS, SaaS and the shared-responsibility model
Build a small multi-tier deployment on a cloud provider
Estimate and control cloud cost
projects: A three-tier application deployed to one provider
A cost and architecture comparison across providers

25.summary: Containers, images and Docker, then Kubernetes and the surrounding orchestration ecosystem.

Write efficient, secure Dockerfiles
Deploy and operate an application on Kubernetes
projects: A multi-container application with Compose
A Kubernetes deployment with health checks and autoscaling

26.summary: DevOps culture and practice: CI/CD, infrastructure as code, infrastructure management and advanced DevOps.
outcomes: Build a CI/CD pipeline from commit to deployment
Manage infrastructure with code and review it like code
Release safely with progressive delivery
projects: A pipeline that builds, tests and deploys a container
Infrastructure as code for a small environment

27.summary: Reliability as an engineering discipline: service-level objectives, error budgets, incident response, capacity and toil reduction.
outcomes: Define SLIs and SLOs for a service
Run an incident and write a blameless post-mortem
Reduce toil through automation
projects: An SLO dashboard and alert policy for a demo service
A game-day exercise with a written post-mortem

28.summary: Metrics, logs and traces, alerting, dashboards and the tooling that makes running systems understandable.
outcomes: Instrument a service with metrics, logs and traces
Design alerts that signal real problems
Control telemetry cost and cardinality
projects: An OpenTelemetry-instrumented service
A dashboard and alert set for a demo application

29.summary: Measuring and improving performance: profiling, benchmarking, load and stress testing, tuning across the stack and capacity.
outcomes: Profile before optimising
Design a load test and read its results
Identify CPU, memory, I/O and lock bottlenecks
projects: A profiling report for a slow program with before-and-after measurements
A load test of a small API

30.summary: Testing fundamentals, levels and types, advanced testing, test frameworks and quality engineering.
outcomes: Design effective unit, integration and end-to-end tests
Use mocks, fixtures and property-based testing appropriately
Measure and improve test quality
projects: A test suite with measured coverage for an existing library
A property-based test for a data structure

31.summary: Security fundamentals, cryptography, application security, secure development, infrastructure security, security operations, advanced security and the major standards.
outcomes: Threat-model a system
Avoid the common application vulnerabilities
Use cryptographic primitives correctly, and know when not to build your own
projects: A threat model for a small web application
A secure authentication flow with documented attack analysis

32.summary: Data fundamentals and processing, pipeline architecture, big data, streaming, modern data architectures, orchestration and advanced data engineering.
outcomes: Design batch and streaming pipelines
Choose among warehouses, lakes and lakehouses
Make pipelines idempotent and observable

Communicate findings with appropriate visualisations
Frame business questions as analyses

A BI dashboard with defined metrics

Use probability to reason about uncertainty and likelihood

An end-to-end tabular model with a proper evaluation protocol

outcomes: Implement backpropagation by hand for a small network

Explain word and sentence embeddings
Evaluate NLP systems properly

outcomes: Apply classical image processing
Train and evaluate an image classifier
Explain detection and segmentation pipelines

An object-detection demo with an evaluation report

outcomes: Formulate a problem as an MDP

A policy-gradient agent for a simple control task

Choose an adaptation technique for a task

Use a game engine productively

Explain a perception, planning and control stack
